subject: Computer Networking
title: Exchange and ActiveSync
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Exchange and ActiveSync.

hook.text: Corporate email runs on Microsoft Exchange. It syncs mail, calendars, and contacts together.

buildup.text: Exchange ActiveSync pushes new email to phones in real time. No polling needed. Instant delivery.

discovery.text: IT admins can remote-wipe a lost phone's email, enforce PIN policies, and block jailbroken devices.

twist.text: Exchange Online is now part of Microsoft 365. The server runs in Azure, not your basement.

climax.text: EWS and Graph API let apps interact with Exchange programmatically — book rooms, send mail, read calendars.

punchline.text: Exchange owns corporate email. Mail, calendar, contacts — unified.

quiz.question: What can IT admins do via Exchange ActiveSync on a lost phone?
options: Remotely wipe the device's email data

details.summary: Microsoft Exchange is the dominant enterprise email server, providing email, calendaring, contacts, and tasks integrated with Outlook. ActiveSync is a protocol for syncing Exchange data to mobile devices.
details.whyItMatters: Exchange handles the majority of corporate email worldwide. Understanding it is essential for anyone working in enterprise IT or communicating in business environments.
takeaways: Exchange integrates email, calendar, and contacts for enterprises
ActiveSync synchronizes Exchange data to mobile devices
Exchange dominates the corporate email market

faq.question: Why do most enterprises use Exchange?
faq.answer: Exchange integrates seamlessly with Active Directory, Outlook, and the broader Microsoft 365 ecosystem. It provides enterprise features like shared calendars, room booking, legal hold, and compliance tools. The Microsoft ecosystem lock-in makes switching costs very high.

faq.question: What is the difference between Exchange and IMAP?
faq.answer: Exchange is a full collaboration server providing email, calendar, contacts, and tasks as an integrated system. IMAP is only an email retrieval protocol. Exchange uses its own protocol (MAPI) for rich functionality with Outlook, while also supporting IMAP for basic email access.
